tool.excerpt: Four Killed In Houthi Missile Strike On Yemen’s Presidential Palace In Aden | Times Now India Cities Delhi Mumbai Kolkata + 5 more World US UK Europe Asia + 3 more Entertainment Bollywood South OTT TV + 3 more Sports Cricket Hockey Football Pickleball + 8 more Business Personal Finance Markets Companies Economy Lifestyle Relationships Fashion Books People + 2 more Videos India World Shows Newshour + 7 more More Latest News Education Auto Opinion Viral Live TV World US UK Europe Asia Middle East Australia Canada Iran-US War Live Delhi SIR Protest Live Updates IDBI Bank Sale Imran Khan Jailer 2 Movie Review Hilary Swank Navratri Search "Trending" Middle East Four Killed In Houthi Missile Strike On Yemen’s Presidential Palace In Aden Authored by : Samannay Biswas Updated: Oct 15, 2026, 23:43 IST A missile attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on October 15 hit the presidential palace in Aden, resulting in four fatalities and ten injuries. The attack targeted Al-Maashiq Palace, which serves as the headquarters of the government backed by Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the Houthis fired five missiles at the complex. Photo : AP follow us follow us At least four people were killed and 10 others injured after Yemen’s Houthi movement launched a missile attack on the presidential palace complex in Aden, the interim capital of the country’s internationally recognised government, on Thursday, October 15, according to government military sources cited by AFP. The attack targeted Al-Maashiq Palace, which serves as the headquarters of the government backed by Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the Houthis fired five missiles at the complex. The country’s prime minister and other cabinet members present at the palace were unharmed, according to officials cited by Reuters. Witnesses reported hearing several loud explosions in the vicinity, while smoke was seen rising from the area. Houthis Claim Attack On Saudi Military Operations Headquarters The Houthi movement said it had targeted what it described as a Saudi military operations headquarters inside the palace complex, along with weapons depots. The group’s military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the strike was part of its declared policy of targeting Saudi military deployments in Yemen. The claims about the specific targets could not be independently verified
